why_span_is_tiny.source_quote: benchmark/mono_link.py:242-243 : '_, aspect_avg, (el_lo, el_hi) = sigma_tools(sig_json, drone, bp[b]['band_name']) ; sigma = aspect_avg(el) if aspect_avg is not None else np.full_like(d, 0.01)'
why_span_is_tiny.reading: scene_arm uses the ASPECT-AVERAGED sigma, so its sigma has no azimuth dependence at all. Its phi sweep therefore measures the geometry term ONLY.
why_span_is_tiny.corroboration: mono_link measured 0.13-0.22 % R90 span over phi for C_bistatic_L500; this workflow measured 0.1 % (0.011-0.012 dB) for the geometry-only branch through a completely separate code path. Two independent paths agree that the geometry half of the phi defect is ~0.1 %.

geometry_grid.meaning: the LINK-BUDGET spread term was already swept over phi here (7 points); what was never swept is the DETECTION solve (R90/coverage) in stage_solve.

spec_vs_implementation.reading: the spec already declared a 72-point phi axis at 5 deg steps. The implementation only ever evaluated the headline point. The defect is spec-vs-code drift, not an unknown axis. The sweep grid used here (PHI_SWEEP_DEG = 0:5:355, 72 points) is the spec's own grid.

var_budget_db_S7.spec: docs/REPORT13_SPEC.md:42 (S7) demanded sensitivity.var_budget_db={aspect_psi, geometry_phi, altitude, drone} at d={300,1000,3000} and the conditional sub-headline 'aspect dominates above ~1 km, geometry below'. It was never produced.
var_budget_db_S7.definition: dB span of each term at fixed d: geometry_phi = span over 72 phi of -20log10(R1*R2) (sigma held fixed); aspect_psi = span over 360 psi of 10log10 sigma at the phi=90 geometry; altitude = |term(60 m) - term(120 m)|; drone = 10log10(max/min sigma) over the 5 profiled drones at one aspect.

spec_placeholder_cross_check.reading: the spec's illustrative geometry_phi at d=1000 m (1.08 dB) matches the measured 1.087 dB. The spec's aspect_psi placeholder of 0 is wrong by 17-24 dB: aspect is the dominant term everywhere above d ~ L, which is where every R90 crossing lives.
spec_placeholder_cross_check.spec_subheadline_confirmed: docs/REPORT13_SPEC.md:42 predicted 'aspect dominates above ~1 km, geometry below'. Measured: at d=300 m (d/L=0.6) geometry_phi 13.23 dB beats aspect_psi for W1 (7.55) and G1 (9.80); from d=1000 m up aspect wins in all 3 modes.

scope_of_the_geometry_term.finding: the 23.17 dB figure lives at short range. Beyond d ~ 2L the target sees TX and RX from nearly the same direction and R1 ~= R2 whatever phi is, so the spread term collapses. Our R90 crossings sit at 3.0-10.8 km = 6-22 x L, which is exactly why the geometry half of the phi defect measures 0.011 dB while the aspect half measures 18.6-20.6 dB.
scope_of_the_geometry_term.caveat: this conclusion is CONDITIONAL on R90 >> L. At L=2000 m (a spec baseline) or for a dimmer target the crossings move inward and the geometry term is no longer negligible. The phi sweep must be rerun per baseline, not assumed.
